600.author: eshaoliu
600.body:
## Problem

Issue #589 reports two opaque `run_python` failures before the model finds the lmfit 1.3.4 `conf_interval` calling convention. The issue did not include the original exception text. Direct reproduction against lmfit 1.3.4 confirms the likely failures:

- `lmfit.conf_interval(result)` → `TypeError: conf_interval() missing 1 required positional argument: 'result'`
- `lmfit.conf_interval(result.minimizer, result)` on a `ModelResult` → `AttributeError: 'ModelResult' object has no attribute 'minimizer'`
- `MinimizerResult.conf_interval()` → `AttributeError: 'MinimizerResult' object has no attribute 'conf_interval'`

The valid forms are `ModelResult.conf_interval(...)` and `lmfit.conf_interval(minimizer, result)`.

## Changes

- `skills/code-engineer/SKILL.md`: adds a version-sensitive API section before the workflow. It gives the two valid lmfit 1.3.4 calls, names the invalid forms, requires an `errorbars` check, and points to the reference before the first call. The output-handling guidance now asks for the installed version and the exact exception instead of a guessed correction.
- `skills/code-engineer/references/lmfit-confidence-intervals.md`: documents the result-type matrix, the exact observed errors, and the `errorbars` failure condition.
- `skills/code-engineer/references/lmfit_confidence_intervals.py`: runnable Michaelis-Menten example covering both fit paths.

No exception is swallowed, and no successful result is fabricated. The executor and runtime error handling are unchanged.

## Validation

Environment: Windows 11, Python 3.12.14, lmfit 1.3.4, numpy 2.2.6.

The reference example was run directly and through the bundled executor:

```text
lmfit version: 1.3.4
ModelResult vmax: 12.071
ModelResult vmax stderr: 0.091
ModelResult CI parameters: ['km', 'vmax']
MinimizerResult vmax: 12.071
MinimizerResult vmax stderr: 0.091
MinimizerResult CI parameters: ['km', 'vmax']
```

The invalid `lmfit.conf_interval(result)` path was also run through `skills/code-engineer/scripts/execute.py`. It still emits the real traceback and `TypeError`, with `Exit code: 1`, so the documented failure is not hidden.

## E2E user journeys

**BLOCKED.** The agent/`run_python` timeline and local stack require Linux or macOS per `CONTRIBUTING.md`; this session is Windows 11. I executed the library-level example and the bundled executor path, but not the full product journey. The original session's exception text was unavailable, so the reproduction covers the candidate calling conventions rather than the exact transcript.

Partial fix; keep #589 open until the first-call guidance is verified through the agent/`run_python` path on a supported host.

Refs #589

## Release

Release category: release:fix
GitHub label: pending a maintainer; this contributor account has no upstream write access.
User impact: the code-engineer skill now steers the first lmfit confidence-interval call to the correct 1.3.4 signature and requires checking `errorbars`; failed calls still surface the real exception.
Compatibility and migration: none.
600.head: fix/code-engineer-lmfit-conf-interval-guidance
600.title: fix(code-engineer): steer lmfit confidence intervals to the 1.3.4 API

603.author: zhaozhaozz
603.body:
Parallel research agents already share arXiv concurrency/pacing, but later calls could still queue behind a known upstream failure and repeated 406 responses had no endpoint-health suppression. This change shares health and cooldown within one service process, bounds admission and actual attempts, and permits one recovery probe after cooldown.

Fixes #208

## Behavior

- Preserve existing concurrency and request intervals. Governed calls make one MCP attempt, so internal retries cannot bypass pacing while holding a slot. Missing queue limits now default to 8 waiters / 20 seconds, capped by the tool timeout.
- Share 429 cooldown by upstream group and effective endpoint/authentication digest, honoring Retry-After in seconds or HTTP-date. Without a hint, backoff starts at 1 second and caps at 30 seconds. Reject affected waiters immediately and return retry timing instead of independent sleeps.
- Keep request-specific or unattributed 406 local. Three distinct, consecutive, provider-attributed endpoint refusals within one minute trigger source/tool suppression: 30-second initial cooldown, capped at 120 seconds. Repeated identical inputs do not reach the threshold.
- Admit one post-cooldown probe; success restores access, failure continues bounded suppression, and cancellation releases the slot and probe permit. Credential changes remain isolated; other sources continue working.
- Return a short unavailable/blocked explanation plus structured timing, same-kind alternative source IDs and citation/evidence guidance. Never claim an uncalled alternative or unavailable content was retrieved. Sanitize provider metadata and diagnostics. No distributed state, infrastructure or new user controls.

## Validation

Original implementation validation: `ae5f87f0608a008e9ced844d848621071077b983`. The test-only CI follow-up below is validated at current head `36081741f5b064c8874f3e8b7cfa659638b03022`.

| Check | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed / skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Affected Node UT and deterministic broker/transport fault injection | 117 | 117 | 117 | 0 / 0 |
| Bundled Python MCP tests, including HTTP failure attribution and Retry-After | 30 | 30 | 30 | 0 / 0 |
| Production API user journey | 5 | 5 | 5 | 0 / 0 |

Commands: `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm docs:check`, `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`, targeted `node --import tsx --test` for data-source, tool registry, public-biomed manifests and affected API MCP suites, and Python unittest discovery under `services/gateway/tests`.

Documentation validation: 172 files linted, 144 Markdown files link-checked. Static architecture boundaries: 297 package source files checked.

Baseline regression at `87a87dd36e404cdbc809761991e05e21aa911b8a`: after an injected 429, a later agent round returned a queue timeout without shared retry timing. The same regression passes with fail-fast shared cooldown and no additional upstream attempt.

An extra architecture-wrapper run passed 68/69 script tests; its unrelated RACE contract test could not initialize the default uv cache in the sandbox. The standalone architecture boundary checker passes. Full `ci:ut`, `ci:st` and mocked browser `ci:e2e` were not run: validation targets the changed backend and production API path. No real arXiv/PubMed, real models, DRB or Nightly evaluations were run.

## CI follow-up

The first [PR CI run](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40545539309) ran all 5,153 planned UT identities and passed 5,138. Its 15 failures came from test setup/reporting introduced here:

- Fourteen source-health cases failed before reaching their assertions: the CI worker runs from the data-source package, where the relative temporary parent directory does not exist. The fixture now uses `mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "issue-208-health-"))`, matching existing package tests and independent of the working directory.
- The 406 classification test used four `unittest.subTest` contexts. Pytest printed passing subtests, but the frozen-plan reporter requires exactly one call report per identity and correctly rejected the extra reports. The four input combinations and every attribution/sanitization assertion remain in one test method, without `subTest`.

No production code, assertions, tagged reporting rules, retries or timeouts changed in this follow-up. Local validation uses the same collector/executor and package working directories as CI:

| Frozen-plan worker | Planned / executed | Before: passed / failed | Current head: passed / failed / skipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Source-health Node worker | 16 / 16 | 2 / 14 | 16 / 0 / 0 |
| Bundled gateway Python worker | 30 / 30 | 29 / 1 | 30 / 0 / 0 |

`pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` also passes. The original production API journey above tested identical production code at the implementation SHA; this follow-up changes only two test files.

The previous standard-config worker first reported a socket hang up while polling subagents; nine later cleanup failures reported an active-run Project deletion conflict. These journeys and the Session lifecycle are unchanged. [CI run 40607725387](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40607725387) **passes on the current head**, including `merge-gate`, Coverage, and all five mocked E2E workers. CodeCheck and CLA also pass. Counts are taken from this run's frozen plans:

| GitHub worker | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed / skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| L1 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 0 / 0 |
| UT | 5246 | 5246 | 5246 | 0 / 0 |
| ST | 24 | 24 | 24 | 0 / 0 |
| E2E standard-config | 40 | 40 | 40 | 0 / 0 |
| E2E standard-journeys | 53 | 53 | 53 | 0 / 0 |
| E2E governed | 5 | 5 | 5 | 0 / 0 |
| E2E research | 20 | 20 | 20 | 0 / 0 |
| E2E literature | 6 | 6 | 6 | 0 / 0 |

The previous standard-config socket disconnect and cascading cleanup failures did not recur: all 40 cases pass without changes to those journeys, cleanup behavior, retries or timeouts. Real E2E and distribution jobs remain outside this PR profile.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** — `node test/api/source-health-journey.mjs`, production API process and official SDK HTTP MCP fixtures; no in-process API replacement or model calls. Tested SHA: `ae5f87f0608a008e9ced844d848621071077b983`.

| User scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Configure isolated sources and two research sessions | Real API startup and usable local sources | PASS |
| Concurrent 429 and a later agent round | Shared cooldown and bounded return without amplification | PASS: 9 user calls produced 1 MCP attempt; persisted audit includes retry timing |
| Failed recovery probe, then upstream recovery | One probe during continued failure; later real results | PASS: one failed probe, then two successful accesses |
| Request-specific versus persistent endpoint 406 | Request errors remain local; sustained rejection suppresses later calls | PASS: 4 request-specific failures remain callable; 3 distinct endpoint refusals trigger suppression; later round makes 0 attempts |
| Credentials and healthy source isolation | New credentials can attempt; original cooldown persists; healthy source works | PASS: isolated attempt, preserved original cooldown and real healthy-source result; no credentials in audit |

The journey asserts the short unavailable-source explanation and honest blocked feedback. Broker fault injection additionally verifies queue exhaustion/timeouts, cancellation, probe cancellation, recovery with changed failure status, continued source pacing, available scholarly fallback and unchanged citation/full-text evidence boundaries.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: Parallel research avoids repeated waits and calls to a known failing source; diagnostics distinguish throttling and endpoint refusal while preserving evidence requirements.
Compatibility and migration: No user migration. Internal broker queue defaults are now bounded; generic ResourceRateLimiter optional dimensions remain available. State is process-local and resets on restart.

603.title: fix(data-source): share cooldown and bound recovery across research agents

610.author: yuanzhou75
610.body:
ScienceDiscovery currently defaults new Projects and unset skill selection to all, and starting the Swarm backend overrides even a saved selected list with the entire installed catalog. Default application settings to selected and remove that backend-wide override. Preserve explicit all choices and selected-list persistence; installing another Skill must not widen a selected Session.

Related to #582. **This is a partial application-settings correction and must not close #582 or be merged as the complete isolation/performance fix.**

## Remaining Swarm boundary

The pinned Swarm adapter imports packages into a shared native skills directory. A package imported by another Session can still appear in the native catalog. Swarm team-member visibility APIs exist in the inspected source, but the ordinary agent.work.normal path does not automatically inherit those member rules. This PR does not toggle global native skills or replace the full Swarm system prompt to simulate isolation. Request-scoped catalog/tool visibility and actual model-input/TTFT verification remain required follow-up work in #582.

## Validation

- New persistence/catalog-growth regression: 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Verifies selected fallback, empty new-Project selection, explicit selection surviving catalog growth/reload, and explicit all remaining available.
- All 31 selected API dependency/build projects built successfully.
- Updated store and API expectations to require saved selections and deletion-reference protection under both backends, removing the old force-all exception. Linux complete Store plus the new regression: 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped at a1dbf3fd. The complete HTTP API suite remains pending.
- git diff --check: passed.
- Windows UT/ST/shared E2E entry points were attempted and stop in preparation with spawn pnpm ENOENT before selected tests execute. Exact-head Linux validation remains pending.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED/PENDING: no actual Swarm model-input isolation or real TTFT measurement is claimed. Keep this draft pending complete per-run visibility implementation and the relevant startup/settings/concurrent-session journeys.

## Release

Release category: release:breaking
User impact: unset and new-Project skill selections no longer silently enable the installed catalog; the backend no longer discards saved selection settings.
Compatibility and migration: explicit persisted all choices remain unchanged. Users relying on an implicit all fallback must explicitly choose all or select the required skills. No existing saved selection is rewritten. Native Swarm shared-catalog isolation is still incomplete as stated above.

The tested local commit a1dbf3fd671ab4a7205c13eef02572dfef479555 and published head 3ca4913fadb2ab58c606abcb3d5cadf5df77d62d have identical verified Git tree fc6e126a964671261094176950406ac94eec22d3. Publication used the fork Git Data API after Git HTTPS transport failed.

611.author: yuanzhou75
611.body:
Python started from Runner shell jobs buffers redirected stdout until process exit, leaving progress logs empty while a long-running job is active. Set PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 for sandbox, macOS launch, and direct-shell environments. Reserve the variable from persisted shell profiles and document explicit unbuffered progress logging in the Code Engineer skill.

Related to #439. This addresses log buffering and agent guidance only. The requested CPU/RSS/last-output heartbeat UI is still pending; this PR must not close the full issue.

## Validation

- Real Linux bubblewrap/Python reproduction before the fix: 0 passed, 1 failed because the live log was empty. After the fix, scientific execution and shell-session tests: 17 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, including reading stdout before releasing the waiting Python process.
- Executor and sandbox launch tests: 16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- All selected Runner dependency projects built successfully on Linux at eea025dc3ecfaeb7f8605e22b9cfbab84f32d239.
- git diff --check: passed.
- UT, ST, and shared mocked browser E2E entry points attempted on the candidate on Windows: all fail during preparation with spawn pnpm ENOENT before selected layer tests execute. No full-suite pass is claimed.

## E2E user journeys

The regression exercises a real managed Python process launched through the Runner shell sandbox, redirects stdout, reads the log while the process waits, and then releases it. This is a Runner execution-boundary test, not a browser or real-model journey. CPU/RSS heartbeat UI and a full product long-running task journey remain pending. Keep draft.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: Python children inherit unbuffered stdout/stderr so redirected progress is visible while a job is still running.
Compatibility and migration: no stored data migration. Explicit inline command environment settings remain available. Previously captured shell profiles cannot override the Runner default.

612.author: HongyeZhou
612.body:
Inherited standalone JiuwenSwarm settings could redirect ScienceDiscovery setup to another instance and overwrite its configuration. This change keeps the existing variable names but requires `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_OVERRIDES=1` to enable documented overrides, isolates SDK child environments, and resolves stack endpoints from the SD-owned instance. It also adds a reusable Docker persisted-volume restart journey.

Refs #592 and #593. The issue-specific acceptance journeys pass. Keep this PR in draft while the repository-wide failures and environment limitation below are reviewed; this is not an all-green validation claim.

## Behavior and compatibility

- Ignore inherited `JIUWENSWARM_*` controls unless explicitly enabled; even then, forward only documented controls.
- Give SDK processes an SD-owned home and a limited OS/proxy environment. The packaged launcher also strips standalone runtime controls and injects its own adapter endpoints.
- Refuse setup/start/status/env/stop against an existing custom SDK runtime without the SD ownership marker. Do not migrate or delete ambiguous standalone state. Preserve the established SD default and Docker persisted layouts.
- Keep ownership state after an invalid setup value so a subsequent corrected setup can recover.
- Update internal callers, Compose examples and deployment documentation. Direct adapter startup with the JiuwenSwarm executor requires opt-in and both explicit endpoints.

## Baseline and tested versions

- Baseline main: `76b5a44fcc814a5a69adddb8659eccd2afecc0c9`.
- Reproduction on baseline: initialize a disposable standalone instance named `sciencediscovery`, set `progressive_tool_enabled: true`, and run SD setup with inherited `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` pointing there. Setup changes that standalone value to false.
- PR head: `f339de5198b6021d09c679994ae123a7c3e0185d`.
- Product/build snapshot: `fc188c2f`; later commits change only journey drivers. CLI acceptance ran at `76d9d25f`; the Docker journey driver and full browser E2E ran at the PR head. UT ran at `76d9d25f`; ST ran at `fc188c2f`. These are the actual tested revisions, not fresh full-suite runs of every intermediate commit.
- Validation ran on Linux amd64 with a container engine, using disposable SD and standalone roots and a separate unmodified baseline worktree.

## Acceptance and real-service journeys

| Issue / scenario | Entry point and assertions | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #593 inherited env and SDK discovery | `test/api/embedded-swarm-coexistence.py`: pollute home/install/config/data/endpoints/context controls and credentials; repeated default setup must leave standalone configuration unchanged | PASS |
| #593 identifiable same-name standalone configuration | Give standalone different model and agent settings plus a distinct skill; edit those settings while both instances are live; SD configuration, skill visibility and session identity remain separate | PASS |
| #593 occupied ports and endpoint ownership | Run both startup orders with initially overlapping ports; require distinct live PIDs and port groups, correct status/env endpoints and disjoint session lists | PASS |
| #593 independent lifecycle and logs | Repeated setup/start and both shutdown orders preserve the sibling process/state; wrapper log stays in SD's root | PASS |
| #593 supported overrides and refusal | All five lifecycle actions refuse an unowned existing standalone root. A fresh explicitly enabled SD root supports repeated setup, context changes, invalid-value recovery, start/status/env/stop | PASS |
| #592 default Docker persisted restart | `test/api/embedded-swarm-docker-restart.py`: record registry/endpoints, create a config marker and persisted session, restart the same container with the same bind mount, and verify all remain while separate standalone files are unchanged | PASS |
| #592 custom persisted override | Repeat Docker journey with `SWARM_DOCKER_CUSTOM_HOME=1`, opt-in enabled and an SD-only runtime on the persisted mount | PASS |

Representative commands (installation/image paths are operator supplied):

```bash
JIUWENSWARM_SRC=<pinned-sdk> PYTHONPATH=services/adapter/src <sdk-python> test/api/embedded-swarm-coexistence.py
SCIENCE_AGENT_IMAGE=<candidate-image> SWARM_IMAGE_REVISION=fc188c2f python3 test/api/embedded-swarm-docker-restart.py
SCIENCE_AGENT_IMAGE=<candidate-image> SWARM_IMAGE_REVISION=fc188c2f SWARM_DOCKER_CUSTOM_HOME=1 python3 test/api/embedded-swarm-docker-restart.py
```

The Docker journey co-tests standalone registry/configuration files; live standalone service coexistence is verified by the separate CLI journey. Containers are removed after each run. Candidate image manifest: `sha256:5ea87a86db0083407d3f19677b35523dd91c36e04b903f1cacce0b4595616b82`. The build used an uncommitted download-mirror recipe and a cached micromamba artifact verified against the committed digest; locked dependency versions/hashes and pinned SDK source/patches were preserved. The product Dockerfile is unchanged.

## Repository checks

| Command | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `pnpm ci:l1` | 4 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| `pnpm ci:ut` | 5252 | 5252 | 5247 | 5 | 0 |
| `pnpm ci:st` | 24 | 24 | 22 | 2 | 0 |
| `pnpm ci:e2e` | 125 | 125 | 119 | 6 | 0 |
| Baseline `pnpm ci:ut` | 5249 | 5249 | 5246 | 3 | 0 |
| Baseline `pnpm ci:st` | 24 | 24 | 22 | 2 | 0 |

The runner does not provide a separate blocked count in these summaries. One browser identity fails on an unavailable environment precondition, as detailed below; it remains in the six failures. No assertions were weakened and no identities were removed to obtain these results.

### Failure attribution and remaining limitations

- **UT:** RACE dependency preparation timed out; an orphan then held the Python dependency-cache lock; the web-fetch observer timing assertion failed; the host's bwrap lacks `--disable-userns`; and the socket-health fixture hits a readonly database. Research Python units (19 + 16), RACE (1), and web-provider broker tests (13) passed on focused reruns without source changes. Full baseline UT reproduces RACE timeout and the two host-related failures. Rerun success does not establish a deeper root cause for the observer timing failure.
- **ST:** the authoritative GitHub Python-distribution download terminates, and the SDK's 100-concurrent MCP boundary test times out. Full baseline ST reproduces both failing identities. With a task-owned SDK source installation, the SDK contract rerun reports 78 passed, 1 failed and 20 subtests passed; baseline reproduces the same concurrency timeout.
- **Browser E2E:** research 20/20, standard 88/94, governed 5/5 and literature 6/6. Five failures reproduce on unchanged main in targeted browser runs: artifact paragraph width 774 vs <=760; model-wizard width 598.234375 vs <580; missing Skill review draft; Plan count 0 vs 3; plugin candidate count 0 vs >0. These establish baseline failures, not fully diagnosed causes for the last three.
- **Scientific-environment J3:** candidate reports `micromamba setup failed`. After enabling the same scientific-environment option, baseline is also not ready but remains `installing: Downloading and verifying managed micromamba`. This is an environment precondition gap on both, not proof of an identical root cause. The J3 user journey is not verified.
- **Additional live checks outside the 125 browser identities:** reading evolve-design's SKILL.md fails with `unable to open database file`; this also reproduces on baseline.
- The first browser run executed zero identities because dependency provisioning timed out. The reported 125/125 execution is the subsequent run using prepared Python 3.12 and the repository-pinned provisioner artifact.

## Release

Release category: `release:breaking`.

User impact: ordinary default startup keeps its existing layout. Users who intentionally set documented `JIUWENSWARM_*` overrides must add `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_OVERRIDES=1` consistently to setup/start/status/env/stop and stack startup. Custom runtime directories must be fresh or already marked as SD-owned; ambiguous standalone directories are refused. Manual adapter startup must also provide both SD-owned endpoint URLs.

613.author: zhaozhaozz
613.body:
The real-model gates (merge queue L3, daily L4, release L5 and manual dispatch) all reach the model through `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`, which currently takes its credentials from the `nightly-ci-ds` Environment. The `nightly-research` Environment has since been reconfigured to serve `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` (agent model and judge) through an OpenAI-compatible gateway, and a CI run dispatched against it passed its real E2E slice. This moves every real-model gate onto `nightly-research`.

## Move the real E2E jobs to `nightly-research`

`.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`: `real-plan` (Freeze real E2E matrix) and `real-e2e` (the workers) both change `environment: nightly-ci-ds` to `environment: nightly-research`. Both lines change together so the frozen plan and the workers read the same model variables. Nothing else in the jobs changes.

`nightly-research` provides the same names the jobs read: variables `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL`, `E2E_LLM_MODEL`, `E2E_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, `E2E_JUDGE_MODEL`; secrets `E2E_LLM_TOKEN`, `E2E_JUDGE_TOKEN`, `HF_TOKEN`, `JINA_API_KEY`. Like `nightly-ci-ds`, it has no required reviewers and no deployment branch restriction, so merge-queue refs, `main`, tags and dispatch refs keep working.

`.ci/README.md` and `.agents/skills/ci/SKILL.md` name the Environment in use; both now say `nightly-research`.

`nightly-ci-ds` is left in place; removing it is a repository-settings decision once a few scheduled runs have gone through `nightly-research`.

## Validation

On `cc3e23d1` (this branch, based on `main` `939acdf1`):

| Check | Planned | Passed | Failed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CI self-tests (`pnpm ci:selftest`, `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`) | 86 | 86 | 0 |

The self-tests include the credential-isolation policy: every job that reads a model token declares an Environment and excludes `pull_request` events. That policy checks rules, not Environment names, so it needs no change.

UT, ST and mocked E2E were not run locally: the diff only changes the `environment:` of the two credentialed jobs, which never run on pull requests, plus one line in each of two documents. No file those layers read is changed. They run on this pull request in Actions.

Real-model evidence on `nightly-research`: [run 40621157889](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40621157889) (`workflow_dispatch` on a branch carrying the same two-line environment change; profile `merge`, backend JiuwenSwarm). Both real jobs deployed to `nightly-research` and logged `E2E_LLM_MODEL` / `E2E_JUDGE_MODEL` = `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`.

| Job | Result |
| --- | --- |
| L3 real E2E / Real E2E (basic) | Playwright `9 passed (4.8m)` |
| L3 real E2E / Account for real cases | planned 9 / executed 9 / passed 9 |
| merge-gate | success |

The daily (L4) and release (L5) slices have not run on `nightly-research` with this endpoint yet; the first scheduled daily run after merge is their first run.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable for product journeys: no product code changes. The change is which GitHub Environment the credentialed real E2E jobs read, and those jobs cannot run on a pull request by design. Their evidence is the dispatched run above: real E2E PASS, 9 planned / 9 executed / 9 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped.

## Release
Release category: release:internal
User impact: none for product users; CI real-model gates now call `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` through the `nightly-research` Environment.
Compatibility and migration: none; `nightly-research` must keep providing the variable and secret names listed above.

614.author: ink999107
614.body:
A Project could be created from the sidebar but never renamed or removed, so
the name typed at creation was permanent and the only way to drop a project
was to leave the app and edit the data directory. This adds the two writes to
the project fold, using the gestures the neighbouring Session rows already
have.

## Rename from the fold, like a Session

Double-clicking a project's name opens it for editing in place, and the row's
new `⋯` menu offers 重命名 for anyone who does not guess the gesture. The row
shows the Project the server returned rather than the typed text, because the
server is what trims the name and refuses a duplicate. `Renaming` in
`Sidebar.tsx` becomes one union of "project" and "session", so only one field
is open at a time and the input, its Enter/Escape handling and its blur commit
are shared rather than duplicated.

## Delete behind the same gate a Session has

The `⋯` menu's 删除 opens a confirmation dialog — no typing the project name
back, matching the Session dialog. The body states the consequence: the
Project's Sessions, their workspaces and their artifacts go with it. Accepting
calls `DELETE /api/projects/:id` with `confirmationId`, which the server
already requires and already refuses with a 409 while one of the Project's
Sessions has an active run; that refusal reaches the user as a toast and
nothing is removed locally.

When the open conversation belonged to the deleted Project, the app moves the
active project back to the inbox and starts a draft before refreshing the
lists. Without that step the next message would be written to a Project that
no longer exists.

## Tests

`apps/desktop/tests/api-sessions.test.ts` covers the DELETE body
(`confirmationId`) and the PATCH body (`name`) as separate calls, and
`apps/desktop/tests/sidebar.test.tsx` pins the row's two menu items and the
double-click hint. The browser mock now answers `DELETE /api/projects/:id` and
enforces the confirmation-id gate, so a client that stopped repeating the id
would fail rather than pass quietly. A new `apps/desktop/e2e/projects.spec.ts`
proves renaming through a reload, cancelling and then confirming a delete, and
deleting the Project that holds the open Session — which must leave a draft
rather than a conversation whose Session is gone.

## Validation

| Layer | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm ci:ut` | 5252 planned / 5252 executed / 5250 passed / 2 failed |
| `pnpm ci:st` | 24 planned / 24 executed / 22 passed / 2 failed |
| `pnpm ci:e2e` | not completed locally — see *E2E user journeys* |
| desktop browser suite (`apps/desktop/e2e`) | 72 planned / 72 executed / 72 passed / 0 failed |
| `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` | passed |
| `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test` | 564 passed / 0 failed |

The four layer failures are outside this diff, which touches `apps/desktop`
and nothing else:

- UT `packages/executor/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` — this host's bubblewrap
  has no `--disable-userns` (`bwrap: Unknown option --disable-userns`).
- UT `services/api/src/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` — `unable to open database
  file` while provisioning the Swarm trajectory store.
- ST `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` — 300 s timeout while installing
  its pinned release, a download from the network.
- ST `check:swarm-sdk-contract` —
  `test_mcp_boundary.py::BoundaryTests::test_100_concurrent_calls_keep_identity_and_execute_once`
  exceeded its 3 s `client.connect()` wait under 100 concurrent calls.

The two UT failures were re-run on unmodified `upstream/main` in a detached
worktree and fail there identically. The two ST failures exercise Python
environment setup and the Swarm SDK; they were not re-run on `upstream/main`
for this pull request. The GitHub Actions layers are the authoritative run.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED for `pnpm ci:e2e`; PASS for the desktop subset, which is the only one
that renders this change.

Tested SHA: `91dc6ebf`, one commit on `upstream/main` `76b5a44f`. Surface:
browser (Chromium, mocked API), `apps/desktop`.

`pnpm ci:e2e` runs the mocked **web** subset: its stack serves
`apps/web/dist`, while every file in this diff is under `apps/desktop`, so the
layer executes none of the changed code. It is also red on this host for
reasons the diff cannot cause:

- The reporter's ordering guard `FRESH_JOURNEY_MUST_RUN_FIRST` fires before
  any case runs: `test/journey-approval-defaults.spec.ts` (`@isolation:global`)
  is collected before `test/journey-compact-process.spec.ts`
  (`@isolation:fresh`). Both files, and their tags, are unchanged from
  `upstream/main`; the same guard failed on a freshly reset runtime directory.
- `J309 大屏打开产物时查看器放大且正文保持可读宽度` fails
  `paragraphWidth ≤ 760` with 774. The rule is `max-width: 76ch`, and this
  host has no Inter (`fc-match Inter` → DejaVu Sans), so one `ch` is wider
  here than on the machine where 760 was measured.
- `journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts` also failed; it drives the web
  settings surface, which this branch does not modify.

The run was stopped after 81 of 279 cases: the outcome was already decided by
the three failures above, none of which this diff can reach.

The desktop app's own browser suite was run instead, against the same commit:

```bash
apps/desktop/e2e/node_modules/.bin/playwright test \
  --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts
```

| Scenario | Expected outcome | Actual outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Double-click a project name, type a new one, reload | `PATCH /api/projects/:id` with `name`; the row keeps the server's name across the reload | PASS |
| `⋯` → 删除 → cancel | nothing written; the Project and its Sessions stay | PASS |
| `⋯` → 删除 → confirm | `DELETE /api/projects/:id` with `confirmationId`; the Project is gone, and the conversation open inside it becomes a draft in the inbox | PASS |
| every other desktop journey (rename/delete regression) | unchanged | PASS — 72 of 72 cases |

Passed / failed / blocked / skipped: 72 / 0 / 0 / 0.

## Release

Release category: release:feature
The GitHub label `release:feature` is not applied: the account opening this
pull request has no write access upstream, so `AddLabelsToLabelable` is
refused. A maintainer needs to add it; without it the change lands in *Other
Changes* in the release note.
User impact: A Project can now be renamed by double-clicking its name or from
its `⋯` menu, and deleted from the same menu after a confirmation that says
what goes with it. Before this change neither write existed in the desktop
app.
Compatibility and migration: None. No API, schema or stored-data change; the
desktop app uses endpoints the server already served.

614.title: feat(desktop): rename and delete a Project from its fold
